exposure: umbilical artery Doppler pulsatility index (UA PI) less than the fifth centile
women with low UA PI (<5%) vs. women with normal UA PI (≥5% and ≤95%)
outcome: composite neonatal morbidity and mortality (stillbirth, mechanical ventilation, sepsis, intraventricular hemorrhage, and necrotizing enterocolitis)
interval from IUGR diagnosis to delivery
cohort: 25 non-anomalous singleton pregnancies with IUGR and low UA PI (<5%) matched to 100 controls with normal UA PI (≥5% and ≤95%) by gestational age at IUGR diagnosis, from a tertiary-care prenatal diagnostic center
finding: Among IUGR pregnancies, UA PI <5% was uncommon and not associated with improved neonatal outcomes compared to normal UA PI.
